correctness.rationale: For each finite plank family, define orientation budgets R_1+R_2=W and Bang-box coordinate spans X_j. The two-variable rational inequality follows from a concave tangent comparison and is strict for mixed normal coordinates. Monotonicity of the complementary span yields a crossing/noncrossing dichotomy: if R_j is below the hole exterior width, or is equal with an oblique plank, a strict-margin Bang certificate contradicts coverage. This proves min(1,S), rules out oblique planks at W=S<1, and forces the two exterior intervals in each coordinate to be disjointly partitioned by the remaining planks. Closed-to-open approximation is justified by strict positive slack. Exact-rational executable checks pass, but do not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: The principal full-text paper (Bakaev--Polyanskii, arXiv:2611.00379v1, Theorem 2 and Lemmas 3--6) establishes the sharp annulus threshold and the Bang-box proof method. The exact cost is prior-implied from those inequalities and is NOT claimed as independently novel. The new claim is that every optimum with h_1+h_2>1 has coordinate normals and that the complete set of optimum arrangements is precisely the four exterior-interval partitions. In the inspected full text, no such equality characterization appears. value.rationale: The new part classifies all finite exact width-minimizing coverings for every strictly interior rectangular hole whose four canonical exterior strips cost less than one, not merely the cost bound. The result exhibits a sharp change in the allowed optimizer arrangements at the threshold and resolves genuine equality geometry with arbitrary locations and plank directions. It provides a natural structural benchmark for future near-minimizer stability work.
